🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Saturday, 31 October 2026

1. 🚤 Data details small boat arrivals and crossings stopped by France
Published transparency data covers the number of migrants arriving in the UK in small boats.

2. 🏛️ Mahmood expected to announce changes to indefinite leave to remain
The home secretary has faced opposition from within the government over plans to impose new rules on migrant workers already in the UK.

3. 💷 Healey's first budget adds tax charge on savings and property income
In his first budget as chancellor, John Healey dropped a plan to cut the cash Isa limit for under-65s.

4. 🏠 Labour meets pledge to bring in 300 new planning officers
The Labour Party has met its manifesto promise to bring in 300 new planning officers.

5. ☀️ UK could see 10 days without rain as high pressure builds
High pressure is developing across the UK, with no significant rain in the forecast for the start of November.

6. 💻 Binance tries to recover $6.3bn stolen in North Korea-linked hack
The crypto firm is attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in a cyber-attack linked to North Korea.

7. 🏉 England beat USA 55-12 in WXV Global Series after Canada defeats
England bounced back from defeats to Canada with a 55-12 win over the USA in the WXV Global Series.

8. 👑 King and Andy Burnham to face reparations protests in Antigua
King Charles and Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be greeted by reparations messages as they travel through St John's for the Commonwealth leaders' summit next week.

Sources: GOV.UK Home Office, BBC, Guardian, The Independent, BBC Sport. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Chris McAndrew / CC BY 3.0, Wikimedia Commons; White House / Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

items.title: Data details small boat arrivals and crossings stopped by France
items.body: Published transparency data covers the number of migrants arriving in the UK in small boats. It also covers those prevented by French authorities from crossing the English Channel.

items.title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to indefinite leave to remain
items.body: The home secretary has faced opposition from within the government over plans to impose new rules on migrant workers already in the UK. Mahmood is expected to announce changes to the rules on indefinite leave to remain.

items.title: Healey's first budget adds tax charge on savings and property income
items.body: In his first budget as chancellor, John Healey dropped a plan to cut the cash Isa limit for under-65s. He surprised everyone, however, with an extra tax charge on savings and property income.

items.title: Labour meets pledge to bring in 300 new planning officers
items.body: The Labour Party has met its manifesto promise to bring in 300 new planning officers. The deadline for its target of building 1.5m new homes is approaching.

items.title: UK could see 10 days without rain as high pressure builds
items.body: High pressure is developing across the UK, with no significant rain in the forecast for the start of November. It follows what has been described as the wettest week in two years.

items.title: Binance tries to recover $6.3bn stolen in North Korea-linked hack
items.body: The crypto firm is attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in a cyber-attack linked to North Korea. The company describes the attack as complex, and it is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.

items.title: England beat USA 55-12 in WXV Global Series after Canada defeats
items.body: England bounced back from defeats to Canada with a 55-12 win over the USA in the WXV Global Series. Moloney-MacDonald scored four tries.

items.title: King and Andy Burnham to face reparations protests in Antigua
items.body: King Charles and Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be greeted by reparations messages as they travel through St John's for the Commonwealth leaders' summit next week. Activists want the UK to confront its role in transatlantic enslavement.
